project: Titanic opening — source-first historical evidence, 16 original narration-locked images

shots.onscreen_label: THE REAL RMS TITANIC, BEFORE THE SINKING
shots.editorial_why: Contemporary actual Titanic ship photograph establishes the object of the opening, dated clearly as before the disaster.
No photograph of the iceberg warning at 11:40 pm exists. An explicitly disclosed original illustration is the only honest visual.
An evidence-based clock diagram communicates exact time interval more precisely than a generic photograph.

shots.onscreen_label: THE REAL VESSEL BEFORE ITS LAST VOYAGE — 1911
shots.editorial_why: Authentic historical full-vessel photo anchors the many tasks that had to take place aboard, captioned before sinking, not the event.
Contemporary committee photograph supports the narrator's explicit discussion of the American investigation, not a fabricated document.

shots.onscreen_label: BRITISH AND AMERICAN INVESTIGATIONS — SOURCE COMPARISON
shots.editorial_why: The narrator contrasts two inquiries; clearly labelled source summary must avoid creating fake facsimiles, interpret as original graphic.

shots.onscreen_label: AN ARCHIVAL PHOTOGRAPH: TITANIC DEPARTING SOUTHAMPTON
shots.editorial_why: Narration explicitly contrasts true period photographs with later reconstruction. An original 1912 ship image is exactly relevant.
A necessary infographic explains why genuine imagery is distinct from the disaster scenes no cameras recorded.

shots.onscreen_label: REAL TITANIC LIFEBOATS — PHOTOGRAPHED AFTER RESCUE
shots.editorial_why: Original Carpathia-era lifeboat photograph shows actual boats; prominent AFTER RESCUE warning avoids asserting 20-boat count or launch-time occupancy.
The exact figures are best demonstrated as verifiable numbers, not by misrepresenting survivors in a photo as capacity evidence.
Genuine portrait of the rescue captain named in narration; no invented night-rescue scene.
Authentic post-sinking boats emphasize the real rescue vessel; NOT a live emergency-radio-room photo.

shots.onscreen_label: SURVIVORS WERE SAVED — AFTER THE SINKING
shots.editorial_why: Authentic contemporaneous survivors photo illustrates the human stakes of the decision while caption distinguishing aftermath from pre-sinking doubt.

shots.onscreen_label: ILLUSTRATION: A LIFEBOAT OVER THE SEA AT NIGHT
shots.editorial_why: No actual camera shot exists for the lowering decision during sinking; one clearly marked evidence-driven drawing is necessary.
Contemporary departure image anchors the narrated channel introduction in real evidence rather than a generic cartoon end screen.
The second distinct period photo underscores that the series will trace original records from construction, with narrated subscription CTA displayed.

disclosure: 1912 archival images are NOT actual nighttime sinking footage. U.S. inquiry photograph only depicts the U.S. inquiry.
